title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 2 — 4 Main Ideas
subject: ENG-205

cards.term: The three hunts and three temptations
cards.def: On three mornings Fitt III cuts back and forth between Bertilak hunting a deer, then a boar, then a fox in the woods and Lady Bertilak pursuing Gawain in his bedroom, so each outdoor chase mirrors the indoor hunt for Gawain, with the sly fox matching the day Gawain himself turns sly.

cards.term: Gawain's three-way bind in the bedroom
cards.def: Lady Bertilak uses Gawain's fame for courtesy against him until Gawain must "allow her love or impolitely reject it," so Gawain has to stay "courteous and avoid uncouthness" while guarding his soul from sin and not being "counted a betrayer by the keeper of the castle," which shows the knightly ideals pulling against each other.

On the third morning Gawain refuses Lady Bertilak's gold ring but accepts her green silk girdle because she says its wearer "will be safe against anyone who seeks to strike him" and Gawain thinks "it might just be the jewel for the jeopardy he faced," so love of his own life, not lust, is what finally tempts Gawain.

That evening Gawain gives Bertilak three kisses for a "foul-stinking fox" but keeps the girdle secret as Lady Bertilak begged, so Gawain, who stayed chaste and courteous, breaks his sworn bargain and fails in truth (trouthe) at the one point where his survival is at stake.
